issue_context.title: Missing null check and also memory leak of BN_CTX
issue_context.body:
The `BN_CTX *bnctx ` is not null checked after creation or freed before the function returns:
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/59a3e7b29574ff45f62e825f6e9923f45060f142/crypto/evp/ctrl_params_translate.c#L1594-L1609

review_comments:
This one looks like it's even in the success path of the function. Are there any tests that would have caught it? If not, worth adding one maybe?

(Should this also be checking point2buf errors?)

There is no test as it requires trying to obtain a public key as octet string from a legacy key.

The control will return NULL pointer in case of point2buf error. This is sufficient as the OSSL_PARAM_set_octet_string() which is then called in default_fixup() returns 0 if the value is NULL.

> There is no test as it requires trying to obtain a public key as octet string from a legacy key.

Hrm. Are legacy keys tricky to construct? I thought it was just using the old low-level `EC_KEY`, etc., APIs. I see `test_EC_priv_only_legacy` talks about making a legacy key, or is that a different notion of legacy?

I dunno, if this is something that's intended to work, legacy thing or no, that seems worth having tests for.
